questions.stem: Which of the following correctly pairs the vitamin with its IUPAC-recognised chemical name?
questions.explanation: Correct: B₁₂ = Cyanocobalamin. Common confusions exposed by the distractors: B₁ is THIAMINE (not riboflavin — that's B₂). C is ASCORBIC ACID (calciferol is vitamin D). K is PHYLLOQUINONE/K₁ or MENAQUINONE/K₂ (retinol is vitamin A). Knowing the 13 vitamin-to-chemical-name pairings outright is the single highest-ROI memorisation in Biology GK.

questions.stem: The deficiency disease PELLAGRA, characterised by the three D's (Diarrhoea, Dermatitis, Dementia), is caused by a prolonged lack of:
questions.explanation: Pellagra = deficiency of vitamin B₃ (Niacin / Nicotinic acid). Symptom mnemonic '3 Ds' (plus eventually a 4th D — death, if untreated). Niacin can also be synthesised by the body from the amino acid tryptophan, so pellagra is more common in populations whose diet is maize-heavy (maize is tryptophan-poor). B₂ deficiency = cheilosis/glossitis; B₆ = peripheral neuropathy; B₁₂ = pernicious/megaloblastic anaemia — each distinct from pellagra.

questions.stem: Which of the following vitamins are FAT-SOLUBLE?
questions.explanation: Fat-soluble vitamins are A, D, E, K — mnemonic 'ADEK'. All others (B-complex and C) are water-soluble. Fat-soluble vitamins are stored in liver/adipose tissue (so deficiency develops slowly but toxicity is possible); water-soluble vitamins are not stored (deficiency develops faster but toxicity is rare — the body excretes excess in urine). Knowing this split affects both exam Qs and real-life clinical reasoning.

questions.stem: Which vitamin plays a critical role in BLOOD CLOTTING by enabling the carboxylation of specific glutamate residues on clotting factors II, VII, IX, X?
questions.explanation: Vitamin K — the 'K' comes from the German 'Koagulation' — is the cofactor for γ-glutamyl carboxylase, which post-translationally modifies clotting factors II (prothrombin), VII, IX, and X. Without K, these factors cannot bind calcium and clotting fails. Newborns get a prophylactic vitamin K shot for this reason. Vitamin E is an antioxidant; C is needed for collagen synthesis (hence scurvy affects wound healing); B₁₂ supports erythropoiesis and neural myelin — all different mechanisms.

questions.stem:
Match the following deficiency diseases with the vitamin whose deficiency causes them, and choose the correct pairing:
(i) Scurvy — Vitamin C
(ii) Rickets — Vitamin D
(iii) Beri-beri — Vitamin B₁ (Thiamine)
(iv) Night blindness — Vitamin A

options.option_text: All four (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv) are correctly paired

questions.explanation: All FOUR pairings are correct — this 4-way match is the 'canonical' set every student should memorise cold: Scurvy↔C (gum bleeding, skin hemorrhage), Rickets↔D (children's bone deformity), Beri-beri↔B₁ (wet = cardiovascular, dry = peripheral neuropathy), Night blindness↔A (xerophthalmia progresses to corneal damage). A paper-setter using this 4-pair matcher expects students to confidently answer 'All four' — hesitation signals fragile recall.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Vitamin D is unique among vitamins because:

options.option_text: It is the only vitamin humans CANNOT synthesise endogenously
It is synthesised in human skin from 7-dehydrocholesterol upon exposure to UV-B radiation
It is the only vitamin that is water-soluble but stored in the liver
It is produced exclusively by the gut microbiota in humans

questions.explanation: Vitamin D is endogenously synthesised when UV-B (290-320 nm) strikes 7-dehydrocholesterol in the skin, producing cholecalciferol (D₃), which is then hydroxylated in the liver (→ 25-OH-D) and kidney (→ 1,25-(OH)₂-D, the active form). This is why it's sometimes called the 'sunshine vitamin' and also why it's technically a PROHORMONE rather than a classical vitamin. A is wrong (vitamin K₂ and biotin are also gut-microbially produced). C is wrong (D is fat-soluble, not water-soluble). D is incorrect — K₂ is gut-microbial but D is skin-synthesised.

questions.stem: Pernicious anaemia — characterised by failed erythropoiesis and neurological symptoms like tingling, ataxia, and memory loss — is the classic presentation of deficiency of which vitamin?
questions.explanation: Pernicious anaemia is the megaloblastic anaemia caused by B₁₂ deficiency, typically due to failed intrinsic factor production (autoimmune atrophic gastritis). The KEY distinction from B₉/folic-acid-deficiency anaemia is the NEUROLOGICAL involvement: B₁₂ deficiency causes subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord (tingling, ataxia), whereas folate deficiency doesn't hit the nervous system. 'Pernicious' means 'highly destructive' — reflecting its pre-treatment mortality. Supplementing folate alone in a B₁₂-deficient patient can mask the anaemia while letting the neurology worsen — a classic clinical trap.

questions.stem: Which vitamin deficiency is MOST directly associated with NEURAL TUBE DEFECTS (e.g. spina bifida, anencephaly) in newborns, prompting worldwide recommendations for supplementation in pregnancy planning?
questions.explanation: Peri-conceptional folic acid intake (400 μg/day, ideally from 1 month before conception through the first trimester) reduces neural-tube defects by ~70%. Folate is essential for DNA synthesis and cell division — the developing neural tube (closes by Day 28 post-conception) is especially vulnerable. India's 'Iron and Folic Acid' (IFA) supplementation programme for women of reproductive age and pregnant women is based on this evidence. Vitamin A TOXICITY (not deficiency) causes teratogenicity; D and K deficiencies don't primarily affect neural-tube closure.

questions.stem: The term 'vitamine' was first coined by Casimir Funk in 1912 while studying a disease that he cured with rice polishings. Which disease and vitamin did Funk's work directly concern?
questions.explanation: Casimir Funk's 1912 paper isolating a curative factor from rice polishings (against beri-beri) led him to coin 'vitamine' (vital + amine — he believed all such factors were amines; the 'e' was later dropped when other non-amine vitamins were found). Beri-beri was rampant among populations eating polished white rice, which removes the thiamine-rich husk. Christiaan Eijkman had earlier (1890s, Nobel 1929) connected the disease to polished rice in chickens. Scurvy-vitamin C was isolated by Szent-Györgyi (Nobel 1937) well after Funk's coinage; Pellagra-B₃ was elucidated by Joseph Goldberger in the 1910s-20s; Rickets-D was linked by Mellanby (1919) and Elmer McCollum.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the RICHEST natural food source of Vitamin C among the options listed?
questions.explanation: Amla (Phyllanthus emblica / Indian Gooseberry) contains approximately 600-800 mg of Vitamin C per 100 g — one of the world's highest concentrations, eclipsing citrus fruits (oranges: ~50 mg/100 g), guava (~228 mg), and kiwi. In India-specific GK, amla is the textbook answer for 'richest Vitamin C source'. Cow's milk has essentially no Vitamin C; white rice loses C during polishing; egg yolk is rich in fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) but not C — which is water-soluble and mostly plant-derived.

questions.stem: A patient presents with cheilosis (angular cracks at the corners of the mouth), magenta-coloured tongue (glossitis), and dermatitis around the nose. Which vitamin deficiency is MOST likely?
questions.explanation: The triad cheilosis + glossitis + seborrheic dermatitis is classically ariboflavinosis — B₂ / Riboflavin deficiency. Riboflavin is a precursor of FAD/FMN, so deficiency impairs redox metabolism in high-turnover tissues (skin, mucosa). B₁ deficiency = beri-beri (neurological / cardiac); B₆ deficiency = peripheral neuropathy + seborrheic dermatitis + sideroblastic anaemia; B₁₂ deficiency = megaloblastic anaemia + subacute combined degeneration (no cheilosis as presenting feature). The 'magenta tongue' is a dead-giveaway for riboflavin.

questions.stem: Osteomalacia — softening of bones in ADULTS — and Rickets — the same pathology in CHILDREN — both stem from a deficiency of:

options.option_text: Calcium alone, regardless of vitamin status
Vitamin D (and consequent impaired calcium absorption)

questions.explanation: Rickets (children, before epiphyseal plate closure — bowing of legs, rachitic rosary, widened wrists) and osteomalacia (adults, with already-closed epiphyses — diffuse bone pain, pseudo-fractures) are the SAME underlying deficiency — Vitamin D — expressed at different ages. Low D reduces intestinal calcium absorption and renal calcium reabsorption, so bones demineralise despite adequate calcium intake. Pure dietary calcium deficiency can cause similar symptoms in extreme cases but is rare because dairy and leafy greens supply enough; the exam's canonical answer is D. B₁₂ and iron cause anaemia, not bone-softening syndromes.

questions.stem: Which pair of vitamins functions PRIMARILY as an ANTIOXIDANT in the human body?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid, water-soluble) and Vitamin E (tocopherol, lipid-soluble) are the two principal dietary antioxidants — they neutralise free radicals in the aqueous and lipid compartments respectively. Vitamin C specifically regenerates oxidised vitamin E back to its active form, so they work synergistically. Vitamin A has antioxidant-like activity through beta-carotene but its primary role is vision (retinal function) and epithelial maintenance. D's role is calcium-phosphate homeostasis; K is clotting. Thiamine (B₁) is a cofactor for decarboxylase enzymes — not antioxidant.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding vitamin storage and requirement is INCORRECT?

options.option_text: Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) are stored in the liver/adipose tissue and can reach toxic levels
Water-soluble vitamins (B-complex, C) are excreted in urine and require regular dietary intake
Vitamin B₁₂ is stored in the liver for 3-5 years, so deficiency develops slowly
Vitamin C has a large body reserve, so a single month without C will not cause scurvy

questions.explanation: Statement D is INCORRECT — vitamin C is water-soluble with modest body reserves (~2-3 months), and SHIP-bound sailors developed full-blown scurvy within 2-3 months of leaving port without citrus. Even 1 month of near-zero intake can trigger subclinical symptoms in undernourished individuals. Statements A, B, and C are all true: fat-soluble vitamins can reach hypervitaminosis (A and D are the commonest culprits); water-soluble require near-daily intake; B₁₂'s hepatic reserve is unusually large (3-5 years), which is why post-gastrectomy patients can go years before pernicious anaemia manifests.
